newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugoslavia to rechedule London Club debt soon - agency.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslavia to rechedule London Club debt soon - agency.

text.p: Yugoslavia could soon reach a deal on rescheduling its debt to London Club commercial bank creditors, Tanjug newsagency reported on Wednesday.
Vuk Ognjanovic, head of the Yugoslav team for talks with the London club announced the possibility of a "non-standard and favourable model for rescheduling the country's debt," the report said.
London Club creditors had already agreed to postpone repayment of the Yugoslav debt and was ready to offer other benefits, Ognjanovic was quoted as saying.

"Yugoslavia does not ask its debt to be written off," said Ognjanovic. "We are discussing the possibility of converting part of our debt into shares in profitable sectors, i.e. energy, traffic, tourism and agriculture."
Ognjanovic said the talks with commercial bank creditors would resume mid-December.
Yugoslavia, comprising Serbia and Montenegro, is struggling to return to the international financial markets and institutions after four years of U.N. trade and oil embargo.

The embargo, which crippled country's economy bringing it to the verge of collapse, was lifted last October but the so- called outer wall of financial sanctions remains in place preventing Belgrade's access to urgently needed fresh foreign capital.
Included in conditions for Yugoslavia's full return to the international community were cooperation with the Hague war crimes tribunal for Bosnia, and improvements in human rights.
